llm_response.content:
COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: School-level difference-in-differences (DID) complemented by an event–study.

Justification  
• The incentive program (“pay-for-performance”, PFP) was introduced only in 62 comprehensive secondary schools in 1995 while 100+ comparable comprehensive schools were not exposed.  
• We observe two clean pre-program years (1993-94) and two full treatment years (1996-97). The remaining schools provide a natural comparison group and the panel structure lets us difference out permanent level differences with school fixed effects and national year shocks with year fixed effects.  
• A DID needs the common-trend assumption which can be visually and formally assessed with the pre-1993/94 data and an event-study.  
• To compare PFP with the “extra-resources” program (ER) we can run a second DID with ER schools as treated. Because the two programs were mutually exclusive we can stack the data and estimate a three-arm design (PFP, ER, pure controls) or run separate DID estimates and then contrast cost per gained outcome unit.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
• PFP_treat_s = 1 for the 62 comprehensive schools that were eligible for and informed about the monetary tournament beginning February 1995, 0 otherwise.

Control group (counterfactual)  
• The 108 comprehensive secondary schools that were ineligible (either because another school of the same stream operated in the locality or they did not satisfy Ministry criteria) and were not part of the ER program.

Treatment timing  
• post_t = 1 for academic years ≥ 1995/96 (we set 1995/96 and 1996/97 as “post”), 0 for 1993/94 (pre). In the event-study we will treat 1995 (second semester of 1994/95) as τ = –0. If one worries that awards were only paid out after the 1996 matriculation exams we can shift “post” to 1996 and use 1995 as an anticipation year in robustness checks.

Extra-resources arm  
• ER_treat_s = 1 for the 22 schools that received extra hours/training starting 1995/96, 0 otherwise.  
• The control for ER is again the set of non-treated, non-PFP schools.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of PFP (or ER) the treated and control schools would have evolved similarly after 1995. Plausibility: Ministry eligibility rules were largely mechanical (single school of its stream within the town) and are unlikely to correlate with sudden trend breaks in outcomes; we can test pre-period equality of trends.

A2. No contemporaneous shocks differentially hitting treated schools exactly when PFP starts (e.g., local economic shocks, other Ministry pilots). Plausibility: Same national curriculum/exams for all schools; we will verify by controlling for district-by-year shocks or local unemployment rates.

A3. Stable composition of the student body (no selective in- or out-migration triggered by PFP). Plausibility: High-school assignment is largely residential; but we will control for cohort characteristics and check balance in gender, parental schooling, immigration shares.

A4. SUTVA / no spillovers: incentives in treated schools do not directly affect achievement at untreated schools. Plausibility: Teachers rarely teach in multiple comprehensive schools; we exclude localities that house both treated and control comprehensives.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Non-random selection into treatment (treated schools are “single-school towns” which may differ).  
Remedy:  
• Include rich baseline controls and school fixed effects (eliminate time-invariant differences).  
• Show parallel pre-trends graphically and via placebo DID estimates (1993 vs. 1994).

T2. Anticipation or strategic behavior in the 1994/95 transition year.  
Remedy:  
• Treat 1995 as a separate “anticipation” dummy in the event-study and drop it in baseline DID. Robustness: omit or include and see if estimates change.

T3. Spillovers (teachers move to treated schools; students transfer).  
Remedy:  
• Document mobility in the administrative data; include district-by-year fixed effects; drop geographically adjacent untreated schools as sensitivity.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-quality fixed-effect estimators
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading -------------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("israel_highschool_1993_1997.csv")  # one row per school-year

# 2. Variable construction ----------------------------------------------------
# define treatment dummies
dt[, PFP_treat  := as.integer(program_type == "PFP")]          # 62 schools
dt[, ER_treat   := as.integer(program_type == "ER")]           # 22 schools
dt[, control    := as.integer(program_type == "NONE")]

# timing: first full academic year with incentives is 1995/96 (coded as 1996)
dt[, post := as.integer(year >= 1996)]

# DID interactions
dt[, PFP_post := PFP_treat * post]
dt[, ER_post  := ER_treat * post]

# outcomes (illustrative)
dt[, dropout_rate := dropouts_9_12 / cohort_9]
dt[, matric_rate  := matric_certificates / cohort_12]
dt[, avg_score    := avg_matric_score]

# school / cohort controls
controls <- c("avg_parent_schooling", "share_female", "share_new_immigrant",
              "school_size", "share_science_track")

# 3. Main regression ----------------------------------------------------------
# PFP vs controls
formula_pfp <- as.formula(
  paste("matric_rate ~ PFP_post +", paste(controls, collapse = "+"),
        "| school_id + year")
)

est_pfp <- feols(formula_pfp, data = dt, cluster = ~school_id)
summary(est_pfp)

# Three-arm specification (both programs in one regression)
formula_three <- as.formula(
  paste("matric_rate ~ PFP_post + ER_post +", paste(controls, collapse = "+"),
        "| school_id + year")
)
est_three <- feols(formula_three, data = dt, cluster = ~school_id)
summary(est_three)

# 4. Event-study --------------------------------------------------------------
# event time relative to treatment for PFP schools
dt[, rel_year := ifelse(PFP_treat==1, year-1995, NA_integer_)]
for (k in -2:2) dt[, paste0("rel", k) := as.integer(rel_year==k)]
fml_es <- as.formula(
  paste("matric_rate ~",
        paste(paste0("rel", -2:2), collapse="+"),
        "| school_id + year")
)
est_es <- feols(fml_es, data = dt[PFP_treat==1 | control==1], cluster = ~school_id)
iplot(est_es)  # pre-trend visual

# 5. Robustness: school-specific linear trends -------------------------------
est_trend <- feols(
  update(formula_pfp, . ~ . + i(year, school_id)),
  data = dt, cluster = ~school_id)
summary(est_trend)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory predicts positive but modest gains from performance pay when measurement is objective and teachers can respond on the margin (Lazear 2003). Given the size of the bonuses (roughly 3–10% of a monthly salary) I expect:

• Average matriculation rate to rise by ≈ 3–5 percentage points (baseline ≈ 45%).  
• Dropout rate grade 9–12 to fall by ≈ 1–2 p.p. (baseline ≈ 6%).  
• Effects for the ER program are likely positive but smaller per dollar because extra hours may be partially absorbed into reduced class size, an intervention with mixed evidence.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. Parallel pre-treatment trends verified (graph/placebo)  …………………… 1  
C2. No anticipatory effects / policy announced exactly at treatment ……… 0.5  
C3. No time-varying confounders correlated with treatment ………………… 0.5  
C4. No spillovers or interference between units ………………………………… 0.5  
C5. Stable composition of treated and control schools ……………………… 0.5  
Total (out of 5) = 3.0  ⇒ Reasonably credible with the proposed tests.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of plan
